candidates.title: DITTO-X: Forward and Reverse Teleoperation for Dexterous Manipulation and Human Intervention
candidates.finding: The authors describe an actuated hand-agnostic teleoperation interface that aligns the operator's hand with the robot hand before human takeover, with forward demonstrations, reverse state-matched handoff, and DAgger correction loops. Their DITTO-Human public project page separates 847 fully teleoperated, 379 human-intervened, and 662 fully autonomous episodes across six dexterous-hand tasks (1,888 total). These author-reported task and dataset classifications are not HILO residence or keep decisions.
candidates.hilo_adaptation: Propose an explicitly synthetic, non-ranking adapter/handoff fixture that distinguishes autonomous intervals, fully human-driven demonstrations, state-matched human takeovers, and the handback to autonomy. Check source evidence class, intervention start/end/duration, mode transitions, and gaps. Keep actual intervention seconds separate from robot task completion, real resident hours and voluntary human retention. No DITTO dataset ingestion, robot control or license inference.
